# FlowState

> FlowState is a free, open-source (MIT), local-first project memory for AI apps: an MCP server (Python 3.11+, SQLite) that stores todos, changes, decisions, problems and learnings per project in a file on the user's machine. Agents call `start_here` first for a short project brief (quick / standard / deep), record work with `log_work`, find and ask with `search`, and sessions open and close automatically. Twelve tools are listed by default (every name starts with a verb; multi-operation tools are `manage_<things>` with an `action`); the v2.0 tool names still work as hidden aliases. Auto-captured summaries and suggested records wait in a review queue for the user's OK; the user sets the review mode (off / auto_only / types / everything). Deletes go through after a safety copy and undo restores everything removed (children and links too); out of the box FlowState never interrupts the user. When two entries disagree, FlowState queues a disagreement card (keep the older, the newer, or both; the other is marked superseded, not deleted). An agent flags it with log_work conflicts_with or manage_links action=flag_conflict, with up to two short evidence snippets. The review page and the tool reply show the card; MCP Apps hosts can render it in chat. Card taps are not yet cryptographically proven to be a person. Opt-in approvals (`flowstate approvals on`) make an AI's deletes and turning review off wait for the user's own click, and a queued delete lists the exact rows the database will remove (an agent sentence appears only as "AI's note"): a popup in Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code, a phone link through flowstatemcp.com (relay users; the phone talks to the user's own FlowState), or `flowstate approve <id>` in their terminal. Projects have hard rules, handoff notes, todo claims with an expiry (so several agents at once don't do the same todo), cross-project links with change alerts, priorities, subtasks and blockers, edit history with undo, and extractive answers (`search` with `answer=true`). Every recorded change keeps the app, the AI model (only when the app supplies it, never guessed), the machine or workspace and how the app was identified; a "Who did what" view (review page, and `manage_history(action="who")`) lists them. The local/LAN HTTP server takes per-app keys (`flowstate keys add`), so the app name comes from the key. Writes containing secrets are refused. Transports: stdio, and HTTP with a bearer token; optional remote access for cloud AIs through the user's own Cloudflare Tunnel with OAuth 2.1 and per-app tokens, or (v2.2, off unless enrolled) the FlowState Relay: an outbound agent that gives the user's own server an address like https://<handle>.fsmcp.com/mcp, with TLS passthrough so the relay cannot read traffic and data stays on the user's machine. The relay is an optional paid service at https://flowstatemcp.com (10-spot beta; paid plans charge for hosting, never for features); local FlowState stays free and MIT. Every write's answer carries a receipt (record ids and a change id); a write that timed out is reported on the next answer, and an exact repeat within 2 minutes returns the first receipt instead of a copy. Nightly local backups, safety copies before restores, deletes and approved bulk changes, and an optional private-only GitHub off-site copy are built in. An Agent Skill (skills/flowstate) teaches the routine. Many AIs (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Grok) can share one memory at the same time, locally, over the network or from a phone.

Repository: https://github.com/dialectforge/FlowState

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): what FlowState is, quick start, features, commands, tools, honest limits, upgrading (`flowstate update`: signed releases only, automatic rollback) and from v1.1
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): step-by-step install for an AI agent (OS and Python check, setup script, which questions to ask the user, config snippets for Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Grok Build and other MCP clients, HTTP server, backups, how agents should use FlowState, settings, working on this repo)
- [setup_flowstate.py](setup_flowstate.py): idempotent cross-platform setup script, standard library only (venv, database and numbered migrations, client registration with config backups, `--schedule-backups`, opt-in `--offsite-github OWNER/NAME` for private repos only, `--install-skill`, `--verify`, `--dry-run`, `--help`)
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release

## Using it

- Local FlowState makes one network call: once a day it asks GitHub whether there is a newer release. It sends nothing about you or your projects (only what any web request reveals: your IP address). Turn it off with `flowstate update check off`. A newer release shows as one line on top of the brief; agents tell the user once and never update FlowState unless asked. When the user asks, the agent runs `flowstate update --dry-run` in a terminal on that computer, shows the plan, then `flowstate update --yes --user-said "<the user's words>"` (installs only a release whose tag is signed with a key the installed copy lists; backs up, migrates, restarts the services, and rolls back on any failure).

- [AGENTS.md#how-agents-should-use-flowstate-once-its-connected](AGENTS.md#how-agents-should-use-flowstate-once-its-connected): the rules the server sends every client

## Internals

- [mcp-server/flowstate/server.py](mcp-server/flowstate/server.py): tool dispatch, stdio and HTTP transports
